storms.name: Hurricane Katrina
storms.summary: Made landfall in Louisiana on 29 August 2005 as a Category 3 hurricane. The storm surge broke the levees protecting New Orleans.
facts: More than 1,300 deaths
About 80% of New Orleans flooded after the levees failed
Damage of about US$125 billion, one of the costliest US disasters
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Hurricane Sandy
storms.where: Caribbean (Jamaica, Cuba, Haiti) and USA (New Jersey, New York)
storms.summary: Crossed Jamaica and Cuba, then turned sharply north-west into New Jersey on 29–30 October 2012. By area it was one of the largest Atlantic hurricanes on record.
facts: Over 200 deaths across eight countries, including Haiti
Storm surge flooded parts of New York City’s subway and road tunnels
Damage of around US$65 billion in the USA
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Hurricane Maria
storms.summary: Hit Dominica as a Category 5, then struck Puerto Rico on 20 September 2017 as a strong Category 4.
facts: Knocked out Puerto Rico’s entire power grid; some areas were without power for months
An estimated 2,975 excess deaths in Puerto Rico
Damaged most buildings on Dominica
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Hurricane Irma
storms.summary: One of the strongest Atlantic hurricanes on record, with 185 mph (295 km/h) winds for about 37 hours.
facts: Devastated Barbuda, St Martin and the British Virgin Islands
Made landfall in the Florida Keys as a Category 4
Around 6 million people in Florida were told to evacuate
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Hurricane Andrew
storms.summary: Made landfall in south Florida near Homestead on 24 August 1992 as a Category 5 hurricane.
facts: 65 deaths
Destroyed tens of thousands of homes in south Florida
Led to much stricter building codes in Florida
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Typhoon Haiyan
storms.summary: Crossed the central Philippines on 8 November 2013 as one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever to reach land. It is known locally as Yolanda.
facts: Over 6,300 deaths
A storm surge of about 5 m hit the city of Tacloban
Around 4 million people displaced
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Cyclone Idai
storms.summary: Looped in the Mozambique Channel before making landfall near Beira, Mozambique, on 14–15 March 2019. It then caused huge floods inland.
facts: More than 1,000 deaths across three countries
About 90% of the city of Beira was damaged or destroyed
Floodwater formed an “inland ocean” in central Mozambique
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

storms.name: Cyclone Nargis
storms.summary: Hit the low-lying Irrawaddy delta in Myanmar on 2 May 2008.
facts: About 138,000 people dead or missing
A storm surge of about 4 m swept across the delta
The government at first restricted foreign aid
storms.source: Track: NOAA IBTrACS v4 (3-hourly, wind in knots)

earthquakes.name: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
earthquakes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Indo-Australian Plate sinks under the Burma Plate
facts: The tsunami killed about 230,000 people in 14 countries
There was no tsunami warning system in the Indian Ocean
Waves over 30 m high hit Aceh, Indonesia
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Haiti earthquake
earthquakes.boundaryText: Conservative: the Caribbean and North American plates slide past each other
facts: Estimates of deaths range from about 100,000 to over 300,000
Around 1.5 million people made homeless
Only 13 km deep and about 25 km from the capital
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Chile earthquake
earthquakes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Nazca Plate sinks under the South American Plate
facts: About 525 deaths, far fewer than in Haiti
Released about 500 times more energy than the Haiti earthquake
Strict building codes limited building collapses
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Christchurch earthquake
earthquakes.boundaryText: Near the Pacific–Australian plate boundary (Alpine Fault zone)
facts: 185 deaths
Liquefaction damaged large parts of the city
Much of the central business district had to be demolished
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 3.5+ within 100 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami
earthquakes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Pacific Plate sinks under the plate Japan sits on
facts: About 18,500 people dead or missing, mostly from the tsunami
Tsunami waves reached about 40 m high in places
Caused the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear disaster
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Nepal (Gorkha) earthquake
earthquakes.boundaryText: Collision: the Indian Plate pushes into the Eurasian Plate, building the Himalayas
facts: Nearly 9,000 deaths
Triggered deadly avalanches on Mount Everest
Over 500,000 homes destroyed
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: L’Aquila earthquake
earthquakes.boundaryText: Near the Africa–Eurasia plate boundary; the crust under the Apennines is being stretched
facts: 309 deaths
Many older buildings collapsed in the historic centre
Six scientists were convicted of manslaughter; their convictions were later overturned
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

earthquakes.name: Turkey–Syria earthquakes
earthquakes.boundaryText: Conservative: the Anatolian and Arabian plates slide past each other on the East Anatolian Fault
facts: Over 50,000 deaths in Turkey and Syria
A second earthquake of magnitude 7.5 struck about nine hours later
Thousands of buildings collapsed despite building codes
earthquakes.source: Earthquakes: USGS catalogue (magnitude 4.5+ within 400 km, 30 days)

volcanoes.name: Mount St Helens
volcanoes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Juan de Fuca Plate sinks under the North American Plate
facts: 57 deaths
The north side collapsed in the largest landslide ever recorded
Ash fell across 11 US states

volcanoes.name: Mount Pinatubo
volcanoes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Eurasian Plate sinks under the Philippine Mobile Belt
facts: The second-largest eruption of the 20th century
Evacuations saved thousands of lives; about 850 people died
Its sulphur dioxide cooled global temperatures by about 0.5°C

volcanoes.name: Soufrière Hills, Montserrat
volcanoes.boundaryText: Destructive: the North American Plate sinks under the Caribbean Plate
facts: 19 people killed by pyroclastic flows in June 1997
The capital, Plymouth, was buried and abandoned
About two-thirds of the population left the island

volcanoes.name: Eyjafjallajökull
volcanoes.boundaryText: Constructive: the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the North American and Eurasian plates move apart
facts: No deaths
Its ash cloud closed much of European airspace for about six days
About 100,000 flights were cancelled

volcanoes.name: Nyiragongo
volcanoes.where: Near Goma, Democratic Republic of the Congo
volcanoes.boundaryText: Constructive: the East African Rift, where Africa is slowly splitting apart
facts: Fast lava flows ran into the city of Goma
Around 400,000 people fled
Over 100 deaths

volcanoes.name: Hunga Tonga–Hunga Haʻapai
volcanoes.boundaryText: Destructive: the Pacific Plate sinks under the Tonga Plate
facts: The most explosive eruption recorded with modern instruments
Its plume reached about 57 km high, into the mesosphere
Its tsunami reached Peru, Japan and the USA
